one_liner: Header-only SIMD index/tape JSON parser for C++26 on the micron runtime, ~9-31x faster than nlohmann::json.
what_it_does: cjson is a header-only C++26 JSON library: SIMD structural parsing, validation, minification and serialization, plus an on-demand iterator, an RFC 8259 dom with in-place mutation, a lazy functional pipeline layer (fmap/filter/fold), and a consteval comptime mode. Its API is not a drop-in for nlohmann: parse() returns a move-only doc/val handle over a flat index/tape (offsets into the source buffer, strings unescaped lazily) instead of an owning tree of std::string/vector/map nodes; there is also parse_insitu (rewrites the input buffer in place) and a separate builder type for writing output. It depends solely on the author's own 'micron' core library in place of the C++ STL and libc.
how_it_is_fast: Two-stage SIMD engine: stage 1 scans 64-byte blocks to build structural indexes, quote/escape masks, and validate UTF-8 in one sweep (SSSE3/AVX2+PCLMUL on amd64, NEON on aarch64/armv7, a SWAR fallback elsewhere); stage 2 is a scalar FSM building a contiguous 16-byte value arena, i.e. a flat tape rather than a DOM tree. Strings stay as {offset,length} spans with lazy unescape and linear-scan object lookup, avoiding per-node allocation entirely; the 'cjson-reuse' variant additionally amortizes allocation by reusing a warm scratch buffer across calls. This is the same index/tape design used by simdjson-dom and yyjson (which is why cjson tracks those two closely), and it is what produces the large margin over owning-tree parsers like nlohmann, RapidJSON, Boost.JSON and glz::generic.
when_to_use: Hot-path parse/extract of JSON from 64KB to tens of MB where an index/tape handle (not an owning, freely-mutable tree) is acceptable
Already targeting C++26 on GCC and willing to build against the micron core library instead of STL/libc
Need SIMD parsing on amd64 (SSSE3/AVX2+PCLMUL), aarch64/armv7 NEON, or a portable SWAR fallback, and can fix the build to one target ISA
Want compile-time (consteval) JSON parsing/validation baked into a binary, e.g. static config literals
Serialize-heavy workloads where cjson-reuse is claimed 2-3x over yyjson on twitter/1MB/5MB documents
when_not_to_use: Need a drop-in nlohmann::json replacement with a fully owning, freely-mutable std::string/vector/map tree
Cannot take on a second core library (micron) or cannot leave the C++ STL/libc; README states no traditional STL support
Need a single binary that runs across AVX2 and non-AVX2 hosts -- no runtime CPU dispatch is provided
Need proven maturity: repo is about 7 weeks old, 2 stars, 1 open issue, single author, no third-party reproduction of the benchmark numbers
Object-heavy or numeric corpora where cjson-reuse still trails simdjson-dom(warm), e.g. canada.json 0.55 vs 0.73 GB/s and numbers.json 0.61 vs 0.82 GB/s -- pick simdjson there instead

integration.dependencies: micron core library (github.com/rfgplk/micron.cpp) only; no STL, no libc
integration.min_toolchain: C++26; README states 'GCC 16+', INSTALL states 'g++ >= 14 (cjson uses -std=c++26 and `if consteval`)' -- the two documents disagree on the minimum GCC version
integration.platforms: x86-64 (SSSE3, AVX2+PCLMUL), aarch64 (NEON), armv7 (NEON), portable SWAR fallback; no runtime CPU dispatch, so a binary built with AVX2 requires AVX2 at runtime
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial -- explain: conceptually similar one-shot/DOM surface (parse/get/iterate) but different types and ownership model (index/tape doc vs nlohmann's owning tree) plus a mandatory micron dependency; not a header-swap replacement

gotchas: Adopting cjson means leaving the C++ STL/libc for the micron core library -- a whole-program dependency change, not just adding a header
No runtime CPU dispatch: a binary built for AVX2 will not run correctly on non-AVX2 hardware
Erasing an object member does not reclaim its pool bytes, and a warm scratch buffer holds memory proportional to the largest document it has seen until release()

Glaze's own author opened issue #2 arguing the DOM benchmark rows compare cjson against glz::generic (Glaze's schema-less owning-tree fallback), not Glaze's reflection-based fast path; this dispute is about the Glaze rows specifically, not the nlohmann numbers
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick cjson over json.cpp, DAW JSON Link, or Tachyon.JSON when you want simdjson-class index/tape throughput (it tracks simdjson-dom within about 1x on several sizes) plus a native consteval parse mode and a lazy functional pipeline; those siblings stay on an STL-based, nlohmann-like data model, while cjson requires leaving the STL for micron.
verified_claims_summary: On the author's own benches/corpus_vs.cpp (GCC 16.1.1, -O3 -march=native -flto -ffat-lto-objects, AMD Ryzen 7 3700U, taskset -c 0, medians of 7 runs), cjson-reuse parses 1MB JSON at 2.52 GB/s vs nlohmann::json 3.12.0's 0.08-0.09 GB/s on comparable documents (twitter.json parse/tree: 0.08 GB/s) and extracts fields from twitter.json (cjson-dom) at 2.02 GB/s vs nlohmann's 0.08 GB/s; against simdjson-dom(warm) cjson-reuse is close (1.18x on 64KB, 0.99x on twitter/5MB) and behind on 12 of 18 corpus documents.
